changelog: v60: Question Candidates view fills in the Quality and Category columns, which were always blank. Quality is not stored on candidates — it's computed on demand with check_quality (the same scorer the classifier and promotion gate use). Category is only stamped at review/promotion time, so for un-reviewed candidates the view now infers it via _infer_category (target_category → the candidate's neighborhood topic_type → bank letter), shown with the category name (e.g. 'E (Reflection & Wisdom)') and falling back to 'unassigned' only when nothing can be inferred. Tests added in tests/test_wiki_views.py. v59: Question Queue view shows weekly progress at a glance. Adds a progress bar at the top of the queue ('N of M answered · K remaining'), derived from the same bank-truth answered state as the per-row badges, so you can see how much of this week's plan is done without counting rows. Test added in tests/test_wiki_views.py. v58: Question Queue view shows answered state honestly. The status badge was derived only from the queue item's own delivered/queued flag — but nothing in the answer flow writes back to question_queue.json (ask.py reads the queue but never marks items), so a queued question you had already answered still read 'queued'. view_queue now derives status from the question bank (the source of truth for what's answered): each row shows answered (green), delivered (blue), or queued (yellow). Description updated; test added in tests/test_wiki_views.py. v57: Question Queue view is now human-readable. Queue items store only a question id and a bare category letter, so the dashboard's Question column was empty and the Cat column showed a cryptic letter. view_queue now resolves each row's question text and category name from the question bank (parse_questions/parse_categories): the Category column reads 'J (Vision)' instead of 'J', and the Question column shows the actual question text (falling back to the queue item's inline text if present). Column header renamed Cat → Category; test added in tests/test_wiki_views.py. v56: Fixes two long-standing updater bugs that silently corrupted framework files. (1) run_git returned stdout.strip(), so apply_version dropped the trailing newline from every file it wrote — leaving instances with dozens of one-byte diffs from upstream. File extraction now goes through read_repo_file_at (byte-exact bytes, written with write_bytes); run_git keeps stripping for token/list output. (2) The protection check used prefix matching for all PROTECTED_FILES entries, so the file entry 'config.yaml' also shadowed 'config.yaml.example' — meaning the example file could never be updated (instances were stuck on the pre-v35 version). New is_protected() matches file entries exactly and only treats trailing-slash entries as directory prefixes. Adds tests/test_update.py covering both fixes. v55: Dashboard view clarity pass (feedback from the hamburger-menu review). Every /views/<slug> page now carries a one-line description under its title explaining what the page is and what its data means (VIEW_DESCRIPTIONS, injected after the <h1> so empty states get it too). The Coverage view annotates each category letter with its title in parentheses (e.g. 'A (Origins)'). The Entity Candidates view now shows only entities still pending graduation — anything page-eligible or already mapped to a Focus has a wiki page and is dropped (the redundant Graduates column is gone), so the page no longer duplicates what the wiki already shows. The hamburger menu relabels 'Candidates' to 'Question Candidates' to distinguish it from Entity Candidates. Tests updated in tests/test_wiki_views.py. v54: Wiki gains a hamburger menu of read-only dashboard views. serve_wiki.py adds a three-line menu button right of the search bar whose dropdown is generated from a VIEWS registry (adding a view = one entry), and live /views/<slug> routes that render current state on each request: Focuses (the weekly progress/roadmap saturation bars as HTML, reusing roadmap.focus_fill + progress.verdict), Coverage (per-category status bars), Question Bank (categories with answered markers + coverage bars), Candidates (question_candidates grouped by status), Entity Candidates (entity rosters per type with graduation flags), Question Queue, Source Integrity (manifest + lint findings), Focus Recommendations, a Loop system-status dashboard, and an interactive entity Graph (self-contained vanilla-JS force layout via /views/graph.json: nodes sized by sources_count, filled by focus saturation or entity type, edges weighted by shared sources, click-through to pages). All views are Loop-adjacent and degrade gracefully on empty/missing state; existing pages, sidebar, and search are unchanged. Adds tests/test_wiki_views.py. v53: Adds autonomous-loop drift guardrails. Wrapper choices now reuse authoritative research/focus constants, research-expand exposes the keyless --from-response path, lower-level flags for classify verbosity, process-answer summaries, and entity roster force-empty are surfaced, monthly dry-run previews entity roster refreshes, monthly reports include research and roster output, and docs now distinguish monthly roster refresh from compile-time entity graduation. Regression tests lock the wrapper and scheduled-flow parity. v52: Surfaces learning-loop failures without blocking capture. Daily wiki compile, answer quality scoring, optional readiness refreshes, and weekly classification fallback now append inspectable records to state/learning_failures.jsonl; doctor reports recent learning-loop failures, weekly maintenance includes the same summary, and process-answer --commit stages state/ so answer_scores and related learning state are not omitted. v51: Protects symbolic object rosters from destructive refreshes. Object roster AI outages now preserve the existing roster instead of writing an empty fallback, successful object responses carry forward previously known symbolic objects unless explicitly replaced, and object-answer sampling spans the whole archive instead of only the first sorted answers. Adds regression tests for preservation and archive-wide sampling. v50: Makes the weekly planned queue honest by defaulting the delivery queue to 8 items across the planner, wrapper, and weekly maintenance script, matching the expiration horizon so tail items are not treated as committed daily prompts. README removes premature claims about automatic bank retirement and age-based float; candidate quality gating and planner quality multipliers remain documented. v49: Removes the completed person-roster migration bridge after Dave was migrated to state/entity_rosters/person.json. state/people_roster.json and system/people_roster.py are gone, entity-roster --type person is the only active roster path, and from-response accepts only the canonical entities schema. v48: Person rosters are canonical entity rosters. state/people_roster.json now migrates once into state/entity_rosters/person.json, active compiler paths read top-level entities only, Focus alias enrichment normalizes maps_to_focus against current Focus slugs, and people-roster is only a compatibility alias for entity-roster --type person. v47: Defines the Loop as Lifehug's canonical continuous-learning flow and adds Node/Edge graph terminology. README, AGENTS, CLAUDE, and README.template now distinguish In the Loop, Loop-adjacent, and Out of the Loop; they define Node/Node Type for graph reasoning while keeping Entity/Entity Type as the current product/code/frontmatter terms. Relationship pages represent Relationship Edges rather than generic node pages. v46: Relationship pages now use mention-enriched Focus evidence. plan_relationships keeps dedicated Focus answers primary, but can now graduate a Focus relationship page from enough cross-story mentions when no dedicated answers exist, preserving the dyadic relationship prompt lens and adding regression coverage for Dad-like cases. v45: Candidate operator surfaces now derive status choices from question_candidates.VALID_STATUSES, so list/review/update can inspect needs_review and auto_promoted without wrapper drift. Weekly dry-run now previews candidates-auto-promote before the real weekly job mutates the candidate store or question bank, with regression tests covering status parity and dry-run promotion coverage. v44: Neighborhood readiness now separates generated questions from captured answers. Output arcs track question_arc_completeness, promoted_completeness, answered_completeness, lifecycle counts, and ready_to_draft; progress only labels a neighborhood ready when answered material crosses the draft threshold, while promotion and answer flows refresh stored readiness. v43: Classifier joins the autonomous loop. classify_story now uses the same OpenClaw-first AI route as research expansion, dry-run previews without model calls or writes, classify-all accepts --limit, weekly_maintenance classifies a capped batch of unclassified sources before quality/profile/promotion, and classification files use repo-relative keys with legacy stem-only compatibility to avoid source-name collisions. README/CLAUDE/cron docs now show classification as the structured-understanding layer between immutable sources and reviewable candidates. v42: Wiki viewer renders italics. render_markdown/linkify only converted `**bold**` and `code`, so single-asterisk `*text*` and underscore `_text_` emphasis showed literal markers everywhere (answer labels like *Dave's answer:*, the index subtitle). Added `<em>` rules for both forms; the underscore form uses word-boundary guards so snake_case identifiers and file paths (source_manifest.json, entity_roster.py) aren't italicized. Render-only change; no wiki content is rewritten. v41: Periods read chronologically in the index. The period entity roster now carries an AI-assigned `chrono` rank (1 = earliest in life), set during roster curation (entity_roster build_prompt/normalize ask for and validate it); plan_entities passes it into period page frontmatter (new optional `chrono:` field), and update_index sorts the Periods section by that rank (earliest life stage on top — Childhood → My Teens → High School → College → My 20s …) instead of alphabetically. Pages without a rank sort last, alphabetical within ties; all other entity types stay alphabetical. v40: Stop the updater from clobbering the compiled index. `wiki/index.md` (the life-graph homepage, regenerated by `compile` from the author's answers — title = full_name, leading with the life-story block) and `wiki/log.md` (the author's compile activity log) were wrongly listed as framework_files, so every `update.py --apply` overwrote them with the shipped seed — reverting the index title from e.g. 'David James Taylor' back to 'Lifehug Wiki Index' and dropping the life-story section until the next compile regenerated it. Both are now removed from framework_files and added to PROTECTED_FILES, so updates never touch them (belt-and-suspenders: PROTECTED also guards against historical tags still listing them). wiki/SCHEMA.md stays framework-owned. Also fixes the index section list: update_index printed a header for EVERY entity type whether or not it had pages and pluralized them naively, producing empty/mangled '## Selfs' and '## Lifes_Works' sections — now empty types are skipped and headings use friendly labels (People/Self/Life's Work, mirroring serve_wiki's group labels). v39: Place/period graduation gated by AI + real mentions, not the noisy detector. The raw place detector undercounts real places (Mesa/San Diego show 1 hit though they appear across several answers), so place/period/object eligibility is now the AI's judgment (qualifies), and the 'a few mentions' bar is enforced at compile time against ACTUAL mention counts (plan_entities requires ≥2 real mentions for places/periods, ≥1 for people/objects). People keep their score/answers bar. v38: Entity graduation — the wiki builds out every node of the life graph, not just people. Generalized the v28 people machinery into a typed engine: new `entity_roster.py` (`lifehug.py entity-roster --type person|place|period|object`) AI-curates noisy detections into clean rosters at `state/entity_rosters/<type>.json`, and `wiki_compile.plan_entities` (generalized from plan_people) graduates page-eligible entities of every type into pages from their mentions. Per-type graduation: places/periods on a low bar (a few mentions, noise-filtered), people on score, and OBJECTS on AI-judged symbolic meaning (the cleats, the orange shorts), not frequency. Adopts the standard nomenclature Entity / Entity Type / Focus (primary = the author) / entity graduation across CLAUDE.md, the Page Structure schema, and the READMEs (project, template, and instance). monthly_research refreshes all entity rosters. v37: Fix roadmap-rebuild so upgrading actually promotes the author to primary. derive_roadmap previously preserved the prior label/tier/cap for every focus, so an existing instance's life-story focus kept its stale standard/0.30 defaults on rebuild and never got the v36 primary weighting. The primary life-story focus's system-owned identity fields (label from full_name, tier, cap, deliverable) now always refresh on rebuild; genuine user overrides on other focuses are still preserved. v36: The author is the PRIMARY focus, and self-knowledge is a built-in dimension of their life-story arc. The life_story focus (A–E) is now marked primary, labeled with config full_name, tier 'extreme', deliverable 'book', and a raised cap (PRIMARY_CAP 0.40 vs 0.30) — and the planner gives a primary focus the top base weight (PRIMARY_BASE 1.5, above 'extreme' 1.2), so the person's own life story is the single biggest share of weekly questions instead of being tied with / out-weighted by a sub-project like Etherfuse. The SELF_ARC inner-story functions (self_image, value, fear, contradiction, perception_by_others, growth_edge) are now first-class in the planner: added to STORY_FUNCTION_KEYWORDS (so self-examination questions are detected) and STORY_FUNCTION_CAPS (so they're balanced), and the previously-dead self-knowledge floor now fires on the self dimension WITHIN the primary focus (no separate competing focus). CLAUDE.md/onboarding now frame the author as the primary focus and name A–E as the life-story character arc holding both outer narrative and inner story. v35: Identity moves to a committed profile. Non-secret identity/preferences (name, full_name, timezone, question_time, channel) now live in `profile.yaml`, which IS tracked in git so they travel across machines — fixing the problem where `full_name` was stranded in the gitignored config.yaml. Secrets (API keys, bot tokens) stay out of git in environment variables / `.env` / `config.yaml` (all gitignored). load_config() merges profile.yaml (base) with config.yaml (local/secret overrides, wins on conflict); legacy installs with only config.yaml keep working. New profile.yaml.example; onboarding (Step 8) now writes profile.yaml for identity and config.yaml only for secrets. v34: The person at the center. The wiki now renders the author's own life story — previously orphaned. New `life` page type + plan_life_story() builds a self-portrait hub (title = config full_name, synthesized across all A–E answers through a self-understanding lens: values, fears, contradictions, growth) plus one page per life-story arc (Origins, Becoming, Relationships, Purpose, Reflection). The sidebar leads with a top 'David James Taylor' section (hub surfaced as 'Who I am' + the arcs); a pointer also appears under People. The index is retitled to the person's full name and leads with the life-story block. New config key `full_name` (falls back to `name`); relationship pages still use `name`. The v33 project sub-group field was generalized from `project:` to `section:`. v33: Project sub-grouping in the sidebar. A project category's '(...)' qualifier (e.g. '## F: The Problem (Etherfuse Story)') is now captured and written to the page as a `project:` frontmatter field ('Etherfuse'). The viewer nests those pages under a sub-label inside the Projects group — 'Projects › Etherfuse' — so it's clear which project each page belongs to, and multiple projects each get their own sub-group. parse_categories now exposes `qualifier`; supports any project, not just Etherfuse. v32: Sidebar + header cleanup. Removed the redundant header "Search" link (the search box remains; its placeholder is now just "Search"). The sidebar leads with the content groups (People, Relationships, Projects, Themes, …); the less-important meta pages (Index, Page Structure) drop to the bottom under a divider, and the compile log is no longer shown. The schema page is retitled "Page Structure" via frontmatter so it's editable. v31: Drop "Wiki" from titles. The viewer header reads "Lifehug" (not "Lifehug Wiki"), the schema page is "Lifehug Schema", and the generated index/compile-log headings drop the redundant word too. It's still a wiki — just not labeled that in every title. v30: Collapsible, grouped wiki sidebar. The local viewer's left nav (serve_wiki.py) is no longer a flat list of raw page paths — pages are grouped by type into collapsible sections (People, Relationships, Themes, Projects, …) with a caret, an item count, and friendly titles (frontmatter `title:`, e.g. Dad / Grandma Betty Jo / Katie under People). Top-level pages (index/log) link directly above the groups; the current page is highlighted; collapse state persists in localStorage across navigation. v29: Mention scan orders sources by salience. scan_mentions now ranks matching answers by how often the person is mentioned (descending) instead of alphabetically, so the most relevant sources survive the 14-source synthesis cap. Fixes person/Focus pages dropping important later-category material — e.g. a Focus person's death (category D) was being excluded because alphabetical order filled the cap with early A/B answers. v28: Mention-based people — the wiki grows people pages automatically. A new AI-curated roster (state/people_roster.json, built by `lifehug.py people-roster`) turns the noisy person-recommendation queue into a clean list of real, canonical people with merged aliases, role-words mapped to existing Focuses, and junk dropped. wiki_compile gains `plan_people()`: any page-eligible person (score ≥ 8 AND ≥ 2 distinct answers AND AI-confirmed real, configurable via people_page_min_score/people_page_min_answers) who isn't already a Focus gets an auto person page (origin: mention) aggregated from word-boundary mentions across all answers. Focus person pages are also enriched from cross-category mentions — so e.g. an empty Dad Focus fills in from the many places he's mentioned, while Focus behavior (question arc, planner, artifacts) is unchanged. Roster resolution is keyless on the desktop (`people-roster --emit-task`/`--from-response`) and runs after recommend-focuses in monthly_research. v27: Guard also protects legacy pages. The non-destructive compile guard now recognizes an already-synthesized page by layout (prose + `## Sources`, no `## What We Know`) when the `synthesized:` frontmatter marker is absent — so pages compiled before v26 are preserved on the first keyless compile after upgrading, instead of being downgraded to excerpts before they get re-stamped. v26: Durable, non-destructive wiki compile. The synthesis cache (state/wiki_synthesis_cache.json) is now committed to the repo, so prose synthesized on the compile machine travels to every machine and a page is only re-synthesized when its inputs change. Pages carry a `synthesized: true|false` frontmatter marker, and compile will never downgrade an already-synthesized page to a raw excerpt fallback — on a keyless machine (no cache entry, no draft, no API key) it preserves the last good prose and logs `↻ preserved <slug>` instead of clobbering it. Fixes the bug where a bare `compile` (or process_answer/daily_question auto-compile) on a machine without an API key silently replaced synthesized pages with excerpt dumps. v25: README updated to reflect v24 autonomous quality loop. Candidate lifecycle diagram now shows auto-promote/needs_review/retire flows. Big picture diagram shows quality profile feeding candidate scoring and bank retirement. Three-clocks diagram and script table updated to document auto-promotion step and age-based float. v24: Autonomous candidate promotion. weekly_maintenance now auto-promotes the highest-scoring candidates into the question bank each week with no manual action. Promotion score = candidate.priority x quality_profile.story_function_multiplier. Weekly cap is dynamic based on unanswered question count (1 when bank >120, 2 when 80-120, 3 when 40-80, 4 when <40). Per-neighborhood cap of 1 prevents any single research batch from dominating. Candidates below threshold but above 0.70 are marked needs_review. New statuses: auto_promoted, needs_review. Audit trail: promoted_by, promotion_score, promotion_reason. New CLI: lifehug.py candidates-auto-promote [--dry-run]. Weekly Telegram report includes promotion summary. v23: Fire-and-forget cron pattern. weekly_maintenance.sh and monthly_research.sh now include a telegram_notify() helper that reads telegram_chat_id from config.yaml and the bot token from TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN env or ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json (OpenClaw setups). Queue and progress output is captured and sent as a Telegram message at the end of each run — so OpenClaw crons can fire the scripts in the background and exit immediately with no timeout risk. Silent no-op when Telegram is not configured. v22: Artifact workflow. Adds `artifact.py` and `lifehug.py artifact ...` for occasion-driven letters/posts/chapters: create context packs, emit desktop/Telegram prompts, save versioned drafts, mark finals, and promote final/context artifacts into `sources/artifacts/` with provenance. Adds `/artifact` skill, post template, derived artifact source handling in wiki compile/source integrity, and updater migration for artifact sources. v21: Focus terminology migration. Replaces the legacy Focus-category vocabulary across code, CLI commands, docs, scheduler output, planner state, recommendations, and question-bank structure. Adds `focus_migration.py`, `recommend_focuses.py`, `lifehug.py recommend-focuses`, `focus-approve`, `focus-dismiss`, and `--focus-min-score`; protected implementation state is migrated forward without touching raw answers. v20.2: Monthly research loop. Adds `monthly_research.sh` and `lifehug.py monthly-research` so monthly growth is script-first: compile, report gaps, open a capped set of new research neighborhoods, refresh the self-knowledge arc if needed, recommend Focuses, report progress, and safe-autocommit. v20.1: Weekly maintenance loop. Adds `weekly_maintenance.sh` and `lifehug.py weekly-maintenance` so source lint/fix, quality profile updates, planner queue refresh, gap scan, progress report, and safe autocommit run together outside the daily question path. Source lint findings now avoid timestamp-only rewrites. v20: Source integrity layer. Raw answers and ingested stories get source metadata, manifest tracking, source lint findings, additive corrections/reflections, and all sources (including corrections/imports) compile into the private wiki. v19: Keyless desktop Focus question generation. research_expand gains `--from-response <file>`: paired with the existing `--prompt`, the agent (Claude Code) reads the emitted prompt, writes the questions JSON, and the script deposits candidates + neighborhood with no model call. The /focus skill now documents this desktop path (emit prompt → agent writes questions → deposit → promote), so adding a Focus needs no API key or gateway on the desktop; cron still uses OpenClaw/Anthropic. (serve has no model call and was already keyless.) v18: Keyless desktop wiki synthesis. `compile --emit-tasks <path>` writes per-page synthesis tasks (sources + related candidates) with no model call; the agent (Claude Code) writes each page's prose to state/synthesis/<slug>.md, and the next `compile` consumes those drafts into the cache and assembles the graph — so /compile runs on the desktop with no API key or gateway. Synthesis source order per page: cache → agent draft → OpenClaw/Anthropic (cron) → excerpt fallback. Related links are taken from an optional `Related:` line or inferred from [[wikilinks]] in the prose. v17: Wiki becomes a navigable graph. wiki_compile rewritten as plan→synthesize→cross-link→write: pages are now LLM-synthesized prose with content-derived related links (OpenClaw-first, Anthropic fallback, deterministic excerpt fallback when no LLM), plus auto-derived backlinks and shared-source 'see also' edges. Syntheses are cached in state/wiki_synthesis_cache.json so re-compiles are idempotent and cheap (--no-ai forces offline mode; new wiki_model config key). serve_wiki now resolves [[wikilinks]] to real pages (slug→page index with type-priority collision handling) instead of always bouncing to search. New `/compile` Claude Code/Desktop skill drives `lifehug.py compile` (now with --no-ai/--model passthrough). v16.1: Answer quality loop — implicit richness scoring accumulates per answer; weekly profile aggregation feeds multipliers into planner weights and AI expansion prompts; zero friction. v16: Guided Focus manager. One-shot `lifehug.py focus-new` scaffolds a new question-bank category, registers the Focus, and auto-generates+promotes ~8-12 starter questions (graceful scaffold-only fallback when no AI is available). New `/focus` Claude Code skill and OpenClaw message protocol walk through add/show/finish/tune. Adds category scaffolding (roadmap.scaffold_category) and bulk candidate promotion (candidates promote-neighborhood). Includes v15.1: OpenClaw-first AI routing in research_expand (keyless generation when OpenClaw is running; Anthropic SDK fallback). v15: Focus model + dynamic Focus-weighted allocation + self-knowledge/relational neighborhoods + wiki relationships/self surfaces + progress dashboard + three-tier scheduling.
